newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: BRYANT PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO ALL CHARGES
The alleged Port Arthur gunman, Martin Bryant, has pleaded not guilty to the 72 charges arising out of the killings at the tourist resort in April.
Martin Bryant aged 29 faced the charges, including 35 of murder, in Hobart's Supreme Court this morning.
Two extra charges were added this morning.
Bryant has been remanded until November the 19th for hearing of the charges.
INTEREST RATES CUT MUST BE CLOSE, SAYS BUSINESS COUNCIL
The head of the Business Council of Australia says the possibility of an official interest rate cut must be getting closer.
The Reserve Bank board holds its regular monthly meeting tomorrow, the first under the governorship of Ian Macfarlane.

Business Council president, Ian Salmon, says business activity is flat, with profit margins difficult to maintain, export markets softening and consumer spending being restrained by lack of confidence and high unemployment.
Mr Salmon says it's important that the Government's Budget and Industrial Relations bills get through parliament.
HOWARD DEFENDS POLICY AGAINST FOREIGN DOCTORS
Prime Minister, John Howard's says Australia has the toughest standards in the world on foreign doctors.
Mr Howard was defending the Government's decision to cap the number of doctors by limiting access to the Medicare system for doctors.
On Sydney Radio 2UE, Mr Howard defended the policy against claims that it will give an advantage to migrant doctors.
UNION LOOKING TO MINISTER ON BHP STEELWORKS
The Australian Workers Union says it hopes the Federal Industry Minister John Moore can exert some political pressure on BHP to retain its Newcastle steelworks, at a forthcoming meeting.
Mr Moore is due to meet Newcastle BHP management in the next month when the Minister will be briefed on the current status of the local steelworks.
The union's Maurie Rudd says BHP has to take note of the concerns being raised at a State and Federal level about its commitment to the city of Newcastle .
SEAVIEW AIR CRASH REPORT TO BE HANDED OVER TODAY
The Commission of Inquiry report into the Seaview air crash of October 1994 will be handed to the Governor General today by Commissioner James Henry Staunton.

The Inquiry began in January 1995, examining the Civil Aviation authority's relationship with Seaview Air, following the crash of a plane on its way from Newcastle to Lord Howe Island which killed nine people.
John Lavarick, whose daughter Lisa Atkinson was killed in the crash, says he's hoping the report will result in changes to the aviation industry's regulatory system.
MELANOMA VACCINE TRIALS TO BEGIN
In New South Wales, trials for a new vaccine, which researchers hope will eventually be used in the control of melanoma, are about to begin.
Newcastle-based melanoma researcher, Peter Hersey, says the Hunter Malenoma Unit has received approval to begin clinical trials of the vaccine made up of melanoma peptides.
He says the initial trials of the vaccine will be on people who already have melanoma, to see if the peptides assist in the control of the illness.
Doctor Hersey says if those trials are successful the vaccine may then be used in patients who have had melanoma's surgically removed, to ensure the illness doesn't come back again.
STROKE INCREASES WILL REQUIRE MORE NURSING HOME BEDS
A Public Health Association conference in Perth has been told any large increase in the number of strokes in Australia will put a strain on nursing home bed numbers.
The conference has heard that the baby boomer generation is approaching the age where the risk of suffering a stroke is at its highest.

Doctor Konrad Jamrozik (Yam-roh-zik), from the University of Western Australia, says if there is an increase in the number of patients with stroke, there'll be a need for more long-term care and rehabilitation facilities.
SUICIDE RATE HIGH IN THE AUSTRALIAN CAPITAL TERRITORY
Warnings have been made about a lack of mental health services in Canberra.

Foundation President Brian Ianson says the A.C.T.'s suicide rate could be the worst in Australia and may be set to increase. Mr Ianson says there's been a surge in the number of calls to Lifeline and statistics show an alarming rise in the number of people requiring help for gambling addictions.
Mr Ianson says despite this services in Canberra for people seeking help has declined.
He says that's an opposite trend to what's happening in other parts of the country.
CAVE-IN HERO TELLS OF LITTLE GIRL RESCUED
In Western Australia, a volunteer ambulance officer from Margaret River has told of how he found a little girl buried in the rubble shortly after the cave-in.
Jim Swabrick, who helped dig out the only survivor, 12-year-old Sarah Otto, was one of the first on the scene.
Mr Swabrick says rescuers had been digging through the rubble for an hour before the girl's cries were heard. He told ABC Radio, the girl was trapped between two massive rocks.
GOOD RAIN ALLEVIATES FIRE RISK
The Weather Bureau says good rain fall in parts of Queensland overnight have helped alleviate the risk of fire.
There's been falls of more than 70-millimetres in Central Queensland, with the Bureau saying the best falls were in an area just south of Gladstone through to the Wide Bay.
Forecaster David Alexander says while the risk of fire has eased in the south-east corner, it has now shifted up to the south east tropics.
He says it's the first of the summer storm activity.
FLOODS IN ADELAIDE
Cars have been washed away and business premises have had to be sand-bagged at Verdun in the Adelaide Hills, where the swollen Onkaparinga River has burst its banks.
State Emergency Service (SES) volunteers have also sand-bagged buildings in the Main Street of Hahndorf, because of rising water levels.
And the Weather Bureau says Hills residents can not expect any respite from the rain until this afternoon.
SES commander John Thorn says some roads into and out of Verdun and Hahndorf have had to be closed.
There's also minor flooding at Mount Barker, Meadows, and along parts of the Nairn to Woodside Road.
-- Reuters, Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
